### Observation Log

**Session Date:** 2023/05/26 (Fri) 08:43  
**Session ID:** sharegpt_zvmX9pX_29

1. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Midjourney bot uses a seed number to create a field of visual noise, like television static, as a starting point to generate the initial image grids.
2. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Seed numbers are generated randomly for each image but can be specified with the --seed or --sameseed parameter.
3. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The --seed parameter accepts whole numbers 0–4294967295 and only influences the initial image grid.
4. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Model Versions 1, 2, 3, test, and testp are non-deterministic and will produce similar, not identical, images.
5. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Using the same prompt+seed+parameters in Model Versions 4 and niji will produce identical images.
6. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The --sameseed parameter accepts whole numbers 0–4294967295 and creates a single large random noise field applied across all images in the initial grid.
7. [ASSISTANT_SAID] The --sameseed parameter is compatible with Model Versions 1, 2, 3, test, and testp and produces very similar generated images.
8. [ASSISTANT_SAID] An example of a job run three times with random seeds is: /imagine prompt celadon owl pitcher.
9. [ASSISTANT_SAID] An example of a job run two times with --seed 123 is: /imagine prompt celadon owl pitcher --seed 123.
10. [ASSISTANT_SAID] An example of a job run three times with --seed 123 using Midjourney Model Version 3 is: /imagine prompt celadon owl pitcher --seed 123 --v 3.
11. [ASSISTANT_SAID] Even with the same seed number, early Midjourney Model Versions are non-deterministic, so generated images will look different.
12. [ASSISTANT_SAID] To find a Job's seed number in Discord, react with an ✉️ envelope emoji to a Job.
13. [ASSISTANT_SAID] To get the seed number for a past image, copy the job ID and use the /show <Job ID #> command with that ID to revive the Job.
14. [ASSISTANT_SAID] You can then react to the newly regenerated Job with an ✉️ envelope emoji.
15. [ASSISTANT_SAID] To change seed numbers, add --seed <value> or --sameseed <value> to the end of your prompt.
